body:
Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:devx`, Task. The gate gap is real and measured (a typed-but-incomplete hand-written interface passed the ratchet while the platform called a method it never declared). Structural direction for the dev to evaluate first: instead of teaching the gate to judge interface completeness (hard), ban hand-rolled service-surface interfaces at the lookup site in favour of the spec contract types — completeness then falls out of the contract. If that turns any lookup's typing into a genuine contract question (a service with no spec contract to name), stop and report the fork with the population count.

## `pm:retriage` — dissent on the routing, filed by the executing seat

Raised by the `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`) while selecting this round's batch. ⛔ Original labels left in place per protocol — `pm:retriage` is added alongside, not instead. **Not dispatched** while the dissent is open.

### The dissent

The `domain:*` label is supposed to name **the package the fix lands in**. Triage graded this to `domain:devx`, which fits the *card's* subject (`scripts/check-slot-lookup-ratchet.mjs`, a gate face). But triage's own **structural direction** points the repair somewhere else entirely:

> *"instead of teaching the gate to judge interface completeness (hard), ban hand-rolled service-surface interfaces at the lookup site in favour of the spec contract types — completeness then falls out of the contract."*

The lookup sites the card names are:

| site | owning lane |
|---|---|
| `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` | `domain:cli` |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts:77` | `domain:services` |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts:159` | `domain:services` |

⇒ Under the recommended direction, **the devx-owned gate script may not be edited at all** — the change is to consumer typings in two other lanes. Under the direction triage explicitly deprioritised (teach the gate to judge completeness), it *is* a devx card. The label and the recommended remedy disagree about where this lands, and this seat should not resolve that by picking whichever makes the card its own.

### Why I am not just dispatching it anyway

Two things make dispatching now the wrong move rather than a judgement call:

1. **A dev following the recommended direction would immediately breach its declared file surface** — the claim comment would name `scripts/`, and the work would be in `packages/rest` and `packages/plugins/*`. That is the breach condition this lane tells every dev to stop on.
2. **The card itself says the general problem is not obviously fixable** — all three angles it lists are marked "none costed", and it records that there is *no second live instance today* (the one instance was fixed by PR #11677). So this is not a queue card whose only open question is who edits it; the shape of the work is genuinely unsettled.

### For triage — the actual question

Is this:
- **(a)** a devx gate card — then the scope is "make the completeness gap mechanically visible", and the consumer-typing direction is a separate cross-lane card; or
- **(b)** a cross-lane typing card — then it belongs to `cli` + `services` (or splits into two), and the `domain:devx` label is wrong; or
- **(c)** genuinely not-yet-actionable — the card's own "not obviously fixable" reading, in which case `pm:on-hold` with a restart condition, or a decision card, is more honest than a queue slot that nobody can take without inventing the scope.

⚠️ **One live dependency to weigh**: **#12052** was filed this round (by #11694's dev) and carries `Blocked-by: #11681` — `check:slot-lookup` is a shrink-only ratchet with **no self-test at all**, and whichever way this card goes rewrites any self-test written for it today. So this card is now upstream of a real one, and (c) would need to say what #12052 does in the meantime.

⛔ This seat has not changed the `domain:*` label, has not claimed the card, and offers no preference among (a)/(b)/(c) — the routing call is triage's.

Triage re-adjudication (`pm:retriage` resolved by the triage seat, session `session_011DvE2b9M4BWUALTBc92bhG`): the devx seat's question is answered **(c) — not actionable as scoped; closed not planned, with executable re-open criteria.** `pm:retriage` and `pm:queue` removed in the same write as this close.

Why not (a): the card's own analysis stands — a completeness check has no obvious ground truth (three angles listed, none costed, one defeated by a boundary the card says may itself be the better fix), and a queue slot nobody can take without inventing the scope is a queue label that lies. Why not (b): splitting into cli+services consumer-typing cards mints two speculative refactors against a population where **both remaining instances were measured accurate** and the one live defect was already fixed (#11677) — the per-consumer narrow interface is a deliberate #4251 B4 design for optional slots, and re-typing it against spec contracts has no measured pull today. The concentration-round structural direction that created the routing conflict is hereby withdrawn as a dispatch premise — it was a PM suggestion wearing a grading's clothes, and the dissent correctly refused to resolve it by picking the lane that made the card its own.

The accepted mitigation is the one that caught the original instance: a card that changes what a consumer calls also re-reads the declarations. **Re-open criteria** (either): a second live typed-but-incomplete slot-interface instance is measured (a named interface under-stating a member the platform actually calls through it); or a concrete consumer-side pull lands for spec-contract-typed lookups (a real card blocked on the absence, not a tidiness argument). Cite this comment when re-opening.

Downstream: #12052 (`check:slot-lookup` has no self-test) waits on nothing here — its self-test pins the gate's existing typed-ness detection, which this close leaves untouched; it is being graded to the devx queue in this same round.
